summary:
I've been building an intranet dashboard — one page that watches health across four machines and doubles as a launcher for the ~29 internal apps I've accumulated. Getting it deployed was more interesting than writing it: it runs as a systemd service rather than Docker, on purpose, because its whole job is to reach out over SSH to the other boxes, and a container would need a mounted key, ssh_config and known_hosts copied in just to do what the host user already has in place. The gotcha that cost the most time was almost invisible — a hardened systemd unit with `NoNewPrivileges=true` silently disables setgid, so `crontab -l` came back empty with zero error, making one host look like it had no cron jobs at all when it actually had the same ones as everywhere else.

I also went back and fixed the color palette after realizing I'd shipped it with the default green/amber/red status scheme, which doesn't work for me — I'm red-green colorblind, and measuring it properly (simulating the color-blindness and checking the contrast) showed ok-vs-fail was nearly indistinguishable at that palette. Swapped to blue for ok and crimson for fail, added distinct shapes per status so color is never the only signal, and wrote a test that re-runs the color-blindness simulation against the live stylesheet so a bad palette can't sneak back in.

On the D&D campaign manager, I closed out a note-visibility system I'd been building for DMs — letting them mark parts of their prep as player-visible, DM-only, or "reveal later," so one campaign document can serve both audiences instead of a DM keeping two versions. Along the way I found a real leak in the retrieval layer: re-indexing a document after an edit dropped its visibility tag entirely, and the access check treated a missing tag as "visible" instead of "hidden" — meaning an edit to a DM-only page could accidentally make it queryable by the whole party. Fixed and back-filled on production.

I spent some time this week just measuring rather than building: benchmarked thread counts and memory-mapping tradeoffs on the local model server that runs a lot of this infrastructure, and confirmed the current config was already near-optimal — sometimes the useful result is knowing not to change something.

highlights.oneLiner: Benchmarked llama-server thread counts and mmap tradeoffs on the P100 brain; config already near-optimal
